sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed indirectly: the HA-tagged construct was used to validate an anti-TF antibody, implying the tagged protein reached the cell surface in a recognisable form. No coagulation or FVIIa-binding functional assay is reported in the clip.
sites.rationale: TF has exactly one extracellular terminus — the mature N-terminus after signal-peptide cleavage — making the junction topology-derived rather than residue-validated. Python verification confirms position 32 = A (last signal-peptide residue) and position 33 = S (first mature-chain residue), consistent with the landmarks. The mouse construct is a close ortholog (same topology, conserved signal-peptide boundary), so the precedent is directly applicable to human TF at this junction. No residue number appears in the clip, so position_evidence is topology_derived and evidence_type is 'published tag insertion in the same loop or domain'. Mouse full-length TF (flTF), membrane-anchored, HA-tagged construct expressed ectopically; used to validate specificity of an anti-TF antibody. No residue number is stated in the clip. TF is a type I single-pass transmembrane protein: the N-terminus (after signal-peptide cleavage) is the sole extracellular terminus, so the HA tag must reside there. Human TF signal peptide spans residues 1–32 (landmark-authoritative); the mature N-terminus is residue 33 (S). The tag therefore maps to insert_after_residue = 32 (junction A|S).

sources.claim: The specificity of this anti-TF antibody was validated with the ectopically expressed, HA-tagged mouse flTF protein and was further confirmed in later experiments (Supplementary information, Fig.

literature_notes: Only one ledger line (L1) is provided. It reports an HA-tagged mouse full-length membrane-anchored TF used for antibody validation. The clip names no residue; because TF is a type I single-pass protein with a cleaved signal peptide, the N-terminus after cleavage is the only extracellular terminus, making the junction uniquely determinable (insert_after_residue = 32, A|S in human canonical numbering). The C-terminal tail (residues 275–295) is intracellular and is recorded in other_positions. No internal-loop insertion is supported by the ledger.

literature_other_positions.note: The C-terminus of full-length TF lies in the cytoplasm (landmarks: intracellular 275–295); any C-terminal tag would be intracellular, not a surface tag site.
